stem: A certain kind of firework is supposed to last for 30 seconds, on average, after it is lit. An inspector suspects that the fireworks actually last a shorter time than this, on average. He takes a random sample of 100 fireworks of this kind. Each firework in the sample is lit and the time it lasts is noted.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Give a reason why it is necessary to take a sample rather than testing all the fireworks of this kind.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: It is given that the population standard deviation of the times that fireworks of this kind last is 5 seconds.
parts.text:
The mean time lasted by the 100 fireworks in the sample is found to be 29 seconds.

Test the inspector’s suspicion at the 1% significance level.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: State with a reason whether the Central Limit theorem was needed in the solution to part **(b)**.
